newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real ends flat on continued dlr outflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real ends flat on continued dlr outflows.

text.p: Brazil's real ended steady at 1.0615 reais per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market amid continued dollar outflows, dealers said.
The Central bank sold dollars at 1.0615 reais per greenback in the afternoon to increase market liquidity.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts on Monday showed a $105 million deficit. Last week, net dollar flows posted a $300.3 million deficit.

The market is divided about the next decline in the reais-dollar mini-band. Some dealers are expecting a change in the mini-band between Tuesday and Wednesday, before the four-day Eastern holiday. But others don't expect the Central Bank to move before Monday.

The current mini-band was set on March 17 between 1.0565 and 1.0615 reais per dollar. So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.52 percent. In the last few months, the mini-band was lowered between 0.55 percent and 0.65 percent.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0621 reais per dollar, 0.02 percent down.

In the illegal parallel market, the real fell 1.36 percent to end at 1.115 reais per greenback in a thin turnover due to an ongoing probe into an alleged multi-million dollar fraud involving state and municipal bonds.
